doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The 1933 orchestra dries up in 1934
summary: Carter was working to pay rent, not to hold the band together.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Okay. Why don’t we move on with your . . . we’re still around 1933. We’re discussing your orchestra, and unfortunately, the orchestra did not last much beyond 1933. Beginning in 1934, whatever engagements you had began to kind of dry up. Do you remember this period at all? Were you frantically working to keep this group together, or did you see the writing on the wall?
I was frantically working to pay the rent and keep up the payments on the car.

But I wasn’t frantically working to keep the orchestra together, although I certainly wanted to, but frantic is not a word for me. I was always looking forward and hoping better things would happen. But no, I was not frantically working to keep it together.
